task: T236 independent written proof/domain/source inventory review

source_inventory.absence_scope: Only the pinned folder at the pinned revision, not later or other author work.

findings.global_scaling: Induction gives h_prime_t(x)=a*b^(t-1)*h_t(z), z_t=x_t/b^(t-1). Every preactivation has the same positive factor. Invertible diagonal input scaling bijects full-dimensional complete gate histories, including zero ownership. Draw-dependent finite positive scales are allowed pointwise.
findings.distribution_scope: Recurrent rescaling changes the Gaussian input law under that map and may change input rank labels, masses, coverage and accuracy. Positive input-only scaling or whole-readout scaling preserves same-input labels. Independent row scaling is not the same operation.
findings.generic_depth_two: Fix w with nonzero entries and condition on it. On each first-input half, section u=1 leaves H scalar thresholds. When the active vector is nonzero and projections have independent continuous laws, thresholds are distinct almost surely, yielding H+1 histories. An inactive all-OFF half instead yields two, giving counts 2H+2 or H+3.
findings.probabilities_and_rows: Independent centered Gaussian input entries give mixed signs except probability 2^(1-H); H16 counts are 34 and19 with probabilities32767/32768 and1/32768. Independent spherical directions after Gaussian row normalization still have atom-free projections for H>=2 and positive target norms. Conditional independence from w and independence across rows are premises, not consequences of arbitrary normalization.
findings.pointed_parent: For any full-dimensional fixed gate history, choose one nonzero input-weight neuron at each time. Its signed preactivation normals form a triangular full-rank family. Their nonnegative inequalities imply a pointed closed history cone; the sum of all inward normals is positive at every nonzero cone point.
findings.affine_section_bound: After extrusion by one input, ell(past)=1 gives a convex section of dimension t. Past-origin points have lower dimension and cannot support a new full-dimensional history alone. At most H affine hyperplanes cut the section into sum_{j=0}^{min(t,H)} binomial(H,j) cells. Intersecting with a convex domain cannot disconnect an arrangement cell. Multiply parent bounds from at most two first-step histories. This is an upper bound, not a growth lower bound or higher-depth generic equality.
findings.permutations: Consistent hidden coordinate relabeling conjugates the recurrent matrix and adjusts input/readout matrices, preserving function and masses while permuting words. The actual preregistered within-row entry shuffles and entrywise sign flips are different perturbations.
findings.protocol: The snapshot specifies five Frobenius and five row-normalized draws plus two recurrent perturbations, optional cheap k5, k4 coverage and diagnostic accuracy. Distinct ensembles, runtime-selected depth inclusion, readout replacement, first-index zero-state ties, source completeness and numerical mass assumptions must remain separate. No author plan changed or numerical evidence accepted.

alternatives_not_ruled_out: Training can affect deeper counts and mass concentration despite generic depth-two saturation.
Global rescaling may change probability metrics without changing cardinality.
Aggregation across gate histories can avoid costs of enumerating each history.
Finite floating geometry, source implementation, RNG and completeness can differ from the ideal exact-real assumptions.
